Localization (in-container diagnostic, both arms run twice): (a) cases 1313+1414 (num_spec=1): BOTH arms individually deterministic but diverged on exactly the 4 published path rows (bank rows 0-3, all 48 heads, full dv range), max_abs 2.38e-7..3.58e-7, ~63% of diffs <=1 ULP = fp32 rounding-level codegen divergence, NOT indexing; (b) case 1515 (num_spec=2): legacy arm ITSELF nondeterministic — test-construction write-write race (both batch rows shared spec_state_indices rows 0-15, so b=0 path publish and b=1 zero-accept root publish both hit bank row 0; playbook class 3), confined to row 0 once codegen was fixed. Root cause of (a), proven via TTGIR/PTX + container microbench: the container Triton (3.6.0) does NOT propagate AxisInfo divisibility through tt.int_to_ptr — tl.load(bank_ptrs+pid_l).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.float32)) gets divisibility 1 even with tl.multiple_of/structural-shift hints (microbench: arg-ptr=st.global.v4.b32; table/multiple_of/shift variants=scalar st.global.b32; anchor+addptr-offset=v4). The whole batched kernel then compiled with a scalarized layout (sizePerThread=[1,1], warpsPerCTA=[2,4]; 88 scalar st.global.b32, 539 shfl, 121 shared-mem ops, 65 bar.sync) vs legacy's vectorized layout (sizePerThread=[1,4], warpsPerCTA=[8,1]; 22 st.global.v4.b32, 187 shfl, 32 bar.sync) — different tl.sum reduction trees in _gdn_node_step → different fp32 rounding. POST-FIX codegen convergence proof: identical fp32 instruction histograms (311 add / 254 mul / 165 fma.rn / 132 fma.rn.ftz / 34 sub / 34 ex2 / 11 rsqrt / 11 div.full), identical memory/shuffle/barrier patterns, identical TTGIR layouts; sole delta = 1x ld.global.b64 (the offset-table read). Determinism post-fix: all 3 cases, both arms deterministic + zero diffs, 2 consecutive in-process passes. TRITON COMPILE CHECK: the original tl.pointer_type/int64-table cast DOES compile and run in the container's Triton 3.6.0 (no compile error; verified in the failing runs and microbench) — but it is numerics-breaking via AxisInfo loss, and the shipped kernel no longer uses tl.pointer_type at all (wiring test now enforces its absence in the batched-kernel code). RUNTIME: each container test invocation ~7s wall (pytest 4.3-5.4s incl. JIT); full gate cycle incl. localization + PTX forensics + microbench used a handful of short ephemeral --rm containers (no server boots); host-memory recovery run first via the launcher's recover_host_memory (17->104 GiB MemAvailable, swap 0); docker ps empty at end; 87 GiB available after. byteAB.summary: Replay-kernel byte A/B gate: FAIL -> localized -> FIXED -> PASS (all cases, int-view equality, repeated across two independent container boots). The class-10 warning was real but the mechanism was not FMA-scheduling luck: the int64 pointer-table load lost AxisInfo divisibility through tt.int_to_ptr in container Triton 3.6.0, scalarizing the batched kernel's layout and reshaping every tl.sum reduction tree (~1-2 ULP fp32 divergence on published bank rows; both arms deterministic). Fix = address banks as layer-0-anchor + (ptr-ptr0)//16 offset table through tt.addptr; post-fix PTX is instruction-histogram-identical to the legacy per-layer kernel (only delta = the 1 offset-table load) and all published bank bytes are int-view byte-identical. Secondary finding: the test's num_spec=2 case had a write-write race in its OWN construction (shared bank rows across batch rows; legacy arm measured nondeterministic) — fixed to deployed disjoint-row semantics. The tl.pointer_type cast itself compiles fine in the container's Triton (the named compile check passes) but is numerics-breaking and is no longer used; the wiring test now enforces its absence. No flag-split (2b-excluded) plan needed — the gate is green. 2b is now cleared for the next gate stage per FR13_B1_FIX1_GATE_BIND order: first FR13_EAGER_PACK=1 live boot with within-boot B=1 same-seed repeat (class 8), OFF-vs-OFF floor bracketing (class 11), engagement needles + container flag-state asserts (class 9), FR13_FIX1_SELFCHECK=1 armed on one ON arm, decode_seconds/spec_drafts speed counters on prompts_swe4.json seed 1313 (class 12). Caveat for the bind: this gate proves codegen/byte identity of the batched replay at the kernel boundary on synthetic inputs — it is necessary, not sufficient (offline byte A/B != live, class 8); B=4 changes co-residency and the ON path runs under full CUDA capture (class 6), both covered only by the live gates. 4 files changed (+112/-29), uncommitted on main for the monitor; CPU suite 214 passed/10 skipped; docker ps empty, host memory recovered (87 GiB available).
